title: David Fincher Says He Kept Cliff Booth Scenes While Tightening Dialogue
excerpt:
Fincher discussed refining Quentin Tarantino's lengthy screenplay.
He says dialogue was compressed without removing whole scenes.
body_md:
David Fincher has offered more detail about his work on The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, a Quentin Tarantino screenplay following the character introduced in Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.

The original script reportedly ran about 230 pages, and Fincher had previously discussed reducing it by roughly 60 pages. His latest clarification is that he did not remove entire scenes; instead, he concentrated on compressing extensive dialogue and making the storytelling more economical.

That distinction matters because it suggests an effort to retain Tarantino's narrative structure while adjusting pacing for the screen. The available report does not establish a new confirmed release date.
